page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 240 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, the instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 32 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 45 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware instructions such as AVX, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests, fall into the lower 25% tier. However, the high core count compensates in parallelized tasks, with multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded decompression scaling into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also demonstrate average tier performance, alongside Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

Given its balanced resource allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, the n1-standard-64 is suited for general-purpose workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution but do not require high single-core clock speeds. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, and moderate LLM prompt processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this older-generation hardware profile offers a stable, dedicated resource allocation for legacy workloads and multi-threaded applications where cutting-edge single-core performance is not a primary requirement.
